sources.title: Housing supply and delivery
sources.role: Planning practice guidance on five-year housing land supply and delivery
sources.facts: Guidance distinguishes the standard method, Housing Delivery Test and five-year housing land supply; from 1 July 2026 an additional 20% buffer applies in defined circumstances.
sources.guard: A published supply calculation is authority-level evidence, not proof that a particular site is available, viable, deliverable or permitted.

sources.title: Publishing your local plan housing requirement
sources.facts: LPAs must publish housing requirement data at consultation, examination, recommendations and adoption stages under the 2026 data standard.
sources.guard: A published requirement is a plan-level minimum and is not an allocation, permission, completion forecast or parcel result.

sources.title: National Planning Policy Framework - Delivering a sufficient supply of homes
sources.facts: Strategic policies should maintain a trajectory and identify deliverable sites; buffers and annual updating rules apply.
sources.guard: National policy does not itself establish ownership, site deliverability, planning permission or build-out timing.

sources.title: Local plans: housing land supply evidence (December 2024 Framework)
sources.facts: Deliverable sites must be available, suitable and achievable; outline permissions, allocations, permission in principle and brownfield entries require clear evidence of completions within five years.
sources.guard: Template completion or category membership is not itself clear evidence of delivery, viability or commencement.

sources.title: Local plans: housing land supply evidence
sources.facts: The collection provides separate templates for different NPPF transitional contexts and suggests evidence for allocations and other assumed supply sites.
sources.guard: A template collection is not a validated local dataset, adopted trajectory or site-level acceptance.

sources.title: Housing and economic land availability assessment
sources.facts: The method supports assessment of land availability and does not itself determine whether land should be allocated.
sources.guard: Assessment inclusion does not confer allocation, permission, ownership, viability or deliverability.

sources.title: Housing and economic needs assessment
sources.role: Housing and economic need assessment guidance
sources.facts: Need assessment informs plan-making and links to land availability assessment once the need figure is identified.
sources.guard: A need figure is not a site requirement, parcel allocation, market valuation or delivery guarantee.

sources.title: Plan-making
sources.role: Planning practice guidance on evidence and plan preparation
sources.facts: Plans should use proportionate, up-to-date evidence and distinguish stages, evidence bases and adopted policy.
sources.guard: Evidence used in plan-making is not automatically adopted policy or an exact-site decision.
